Rashi on Pesachim 68a:10:1.english: The wicked - Thus, it is something bad and detested.

Rashi on Pesachim 68a:11:1.english: Then shall the lambs feed as in their pasture - [The] lambs [refer to] Israel.

Rashi on Pesachim 68a:11:2.english: As was said about them - Like that which was promised to them by a prophet.

Rashi on Pesachim 68a:11:3.hebrew: מאי כמדובר בם - מה היא אותה הבטחה? ומפרש לה: סיפא דקרא היינו הבטחה, "וחרבות מחים גרים יאכלו" — צדיקים שהיו עד הנה כגרים ותושבים:
Rashi on Pesachim 68a:11:3.english: What is "as was said about them"? - What is that promise? And [Abaye] explains it: the end of the verse is the promise, "And the ruins of the fat ones shall strangers [gerim] eat" — [referring to] the righteous, [who were] until now like strangers and sojourners.

Rashi on Pesachim 68a:11:4.hebrew: אי כתיב חרבות מחים - ה"א סיפא דקרא פירוש לרישא כדקאמרת, אבל השתא דכתב וחרבות, לאו פירושא דרישא הוא אלא מילתא אחריתי היא:
Rashi on Pesachim 68a:11:4.english: Were it written “the ruins of the fat ones” - I would have said [that] the end of the verse is an explanation of the beginning, as you say; however, now that it is written “and the ruins,” it is not an explanation of the beginning, rather it is something else.

Rashi on Pesachim 68a:12:1.hebrew: אלא - כמדובר בם דרישא, היינו כרב חננאל: כמדובר באליהו ואלישע שהחיו את המתים, כך יחיו כל הצדיקים את המתים. ירעו ורעו — לגזירה שוה:
Rashi on Pesachim 68a:12:1.english: Rather - [The expression] "as was spoken about them" from earlier is [explained] according to Rav Chananel: just as was spoken about Elijah and Elisha, who resurrected the dead, so will all the righteous resurrect the dead. "[Let them] feed" (*yiru*) and "[shall] feed" (*vera'u*) [are cited] for a *gezerah shavah* [verbal analogy].

Rashi on Pesachim 68a:13:1.hebrew: ויעני ושפט בבשן - ושפט הוא אביו של אלישע, דכתיב אלישע בן שפט:
Rashi on Pesachim 68a:13:1.english: And Yanai and Shafat in the Bashan - And Shafat is the father of Elisha, as it is written: "Elisha son of Shafat."

Rashi on Pesachim 68a:14:1.hebrew: ושמת משענתי - באלישע כתיב, על שהחיה בן השונמית:
Rashi on Pesachim 68a:14:1.english: And you shall lay my staff - It is written concerning Elisha, regarding [when] he revived the son of the Shunammite [woman].

Rashi on Pesachim 68a:15:1.english: And He will swallow up death - The angel of death will be swallowed up so that he will not have dominion.

Rashi on Pesachim 68a:15:2.english: Regarding Israel - It is written: "He will swallow up death, etc."

Rashi on Pesachim 68a:16:1.english: And the sun [shall be] ashamed - That it will not shine.

Rashi on Pesachim 68a:16:2.hebrew: יהיה שבעתים כאור שבעת הימים - שבעתי' הן ארבעים ותשע, וכתיב כאור שבעת הימים — ארבעים ותשע כאור שבעת ימים של עכשיו, נמצא עודף על אור של עכשיו ג' מאות וארבעים ושלשה:
Rashi on Pesachim 68a:16:2.english: Shall be sevenfold, as the light of seven days - Shivatayim ["sevenfold," i.e., 7 × 7] is forty-nine, and it is written "as the light of seven days" — forty-nine [times] the light of seven days of now; thus it is found to exceed the light of now [by a factor of] three hundred and forty-three.

Rashi on Pesachim 68a:16:3.hebrew: בעולם הבא - "וחפרה הלבנה ובושה החמה", שלא יהא בעולם אלא זיו, זוהר ומראה שכינה:
Rashi on Pesachim 68a:16:3.english: In the World-to-Come - "Then the moon shall be confounded and the sun ashamed," for there will be nothing in the world except the radiance, splendor, and vision of the Divine Presence.

Rashi on Pesachim 68a:16:4.english: To the days of the Messiah - The light of the moon will be like the light of the sun.

Rashi on Pesachim 68a:17:1.hebrew: ולשמואל - דאמר ימות המשיח אין משתנין משל עכשיו, מה הוא מקיים "והיה אור הלבנה כאור החמה":
Rashi on Pesachim 68a:17:1.english: And according to Shmuel - Who said [that] the days of the Messiah do not change from those of now, how does he interpret [the verse], "And the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun"?

Rashi on Pesachim 68a:18:1.hebrew: כתיב אני אמית ואחיה מחצתי ואני ארפא - כיון שאמר שהמתים הוא מחיה, פשיטא דהמחוצים יכול לרפאות. אלא הא אתא לאשמועינן, דלא תימא "אמית ואחיה" לאו דמתים חיים קאמר, אלא אני אמית את המתים, ואני מחיה וזן את החיים ובורא את הנולדים. להכי כתיב בתריה "מחצתי ואני ארפא" — כשם שמה שמחצתי אני ארפא, דאין רפואה אלא במוכה, כך אותו עצמו שאני ממית אני מחיה:
Rashi on Pesachim 68a:18:1.english: It is written: “I put to death and I make live,” [and] “I wound and I heal” - Since it said that He brings the dead to life, it is obvious that He can heal the wounded. Rather, it comes to teach us this: that you should not say “I put to death and I make live” is not speaking of the resurrection of the dead, [but] rather [means]: “I put to death those who die, and I keep alive and sustain the living, and create those who are born.” Therefore, it is written afterward: “I wound and I heal” — just as the one whom I wounded I will heal, for healing applies only to the one who was struck, so too the very same one whom I put to death I will bring to life.

Rashi on Pesachim 68a:19:1.english: Death for one [person] and life for another - I put those who die to death, and I give life to and sustain the living.

Rashi on Pesachim 68a:19:2.hebrew: הכי גרסינן דבר אחר בתחלה מה שאני ממית אני מחיה והדר מה שאני מחצתי אני ארפא - שכדרך שהן מתים — חגרים, סומים, אלמים — כך הן חיין במומן, ואחר כך מתרפאים, כדכתיב: "אז ידלג כאיל פסח" (ישעיהו ל״ה:ו׳):
Rashi on Pesachim 68a:19:2.english: This is how we read [the text]: “Alternatively: At first, what I put to death I make live, and subsequently, what I wounded I will heal” - For just as they die — lame, blind, [and] mute — so they come [back] to life with their blemishes, and afterward they are healed, as it is written: “Then the lame shall leap like a hart” (Isaiah 35:6).

Rashi on Pesachim 68a:1:1.hebrew: בועל נדה כטמא מת - סיפא דמתני' דלעיל היא:
Rashi on Pesachim 68a:1:1.english: One who has relations with a menstruating woman is like one who is ritually impure due to a corpse - [This] is the latter clause of the Mishnah above.

Rashi on Pesachim 68a:3:1.hebrew: מצורע חמור מזב - למחנותיו כדאמרן, וכן זב מטמא מת:
Rashi on Pesachim 68a:3:1.english: A leper is more severe than a zav - with respect to his camps, as we said [above], and similarly a zav [is more severe] than one who is impure from a corpse.

Rashi on Pesachim 68a:3:2.english: To the exclusion of a person who experienced a seminal emission - [The Gemara] proceeds to explain what this is.

Rashi on Pesachim 68a:5:1.hebrew: לא, יצא מכלל טמא מת כו' - והכי משמע: יצא בעל קרי מכלל זה — דהנך לפי חומר טומאתן חומר שלוחן, יצא בעל קרי — שאע"פ שטמא מת חמור ממנו, שהוא טומאת שבעה וזה טומאת ערב, אפילו הכי לענין מחנות בעל קרי חמור. דעל כרחיך, כי כתיב "וכל זב", לרבויי בעל קרי אתא לכלל זב, ו"כל טמא", לרבויי טמא שרץ לכלל טמא מת אתא; דכל חד וחד למאי דדמי ליה מדמינן ליה, ובעל קרי דומה לזב, שהטומאה יוצאה עליו מגופו:
Rashi on Pesachim 68a:5:1.english: No, he was excluded from the category of one impure from a corpse, etc. - This is what it means: A ba'al keri [one who had a seminal emission] is excluded from this [rule] — for [with respect to] those [other impure people], according to the severity of their impurity is the severity of their expulsion [from the camps], [whereas] a ba'al keri is an exception, for although one impure from a corpse is more severe than him, in that it is a seven-day impurity whereas this [i.e., a ba'al keri] is an evening impurity, nevertheless, with respect to the camps, a ba'al keri is more severe. For perforce, when it is written "and every zav" [Numbers 5:2], it comes to include a ba'al keri in the category of zav, and "and every impure [person]" comes to include one impure from a sheretz [creeping creature] in the category of one impure from a corpse; for we compare each and every one to that which is similar to it, and a ba'al keri is similar to a zav, since the impurity issues upon him from his body.

Rashi on Pesachim 68a:6:1.hebrew: ויצא אל מחוץ למחנה - בבעל קרי כתיב, כי יהיה בך איש וגו':
Rashi on Pesachim 68a:6:1.english: He shall go outside the camp - [This] is written concerning one who experienced a seminal emission, "If there be among you a man, etc."

Rashi on Pesachim 68a:6:2.hebrew: הכי גרסינן: "ויצא אל מחוץ למחנה" — זו מחנה שכינה; "ולא יבא אל תוך המחנה" — זו מחנה לויה; מכאן שבעל קרי משתלח חוץ לשתי מחנות. דקאמר קרא שאם נטמא בעזרה, יצא משתיהן:
Rashi on Pesachim 68a:6:2.english: This is the correct reading: "He shall go outside the camp" — this is the camp of the Divine Presence; "and he shall not come within the camp" — this is the Levite camp; from here [we derive] that one who experienced a seminal emission is sent outside of two camps. For the verse says that if he became impure in the Temple Courtyard, he must go out from both of them.

Rashi on Pesachim 68a:7:1.hebrew: אמר ליה אכתי לא אעילתיה אפיקתיה - עדיין לא הכנסתו למחנה לויה וכבר הוצאתו ממנה. דמדקאמרת "לא יבא לתוכה", מכלל דעומד חוצה לה וקאמר לא יכנס, והא אכתי לא אישתעי בזה שיצא ממחנה שכינה ועומד במחנה לויה לשלחו ממנה, וקא מזהר ליה שלא יכנס כאילו כבר יצא. אכתי לא אעילתיה — כלומר, עדיין לא דיבר על כניסתו מה תהא עליה — אפיקתיה, ודיבר עליו כאילו יצא. ל"א גרסי' "אכתי לא אפיקתיה אעילתי'": עדיין לא הוצרכתו לצאת ממחנה לויה וכבר הזהרתו שלא יכנס, והיינו אעילתיה — כבר אתה מדבר בכניסתו:
Rashi on Pesachim 68a:7:1.english: He said to him: You have not yet brought him in, [and] you have sent him out - You have not yet brought him into the Levite camp, and already you have sent him out of it. For since you say, "He shall not come into it," it follows that he is standing outside of it and [Scripture] says he shall not enter; yet it has not yet spoken of this [person] having left the camp of the Divine Presence and standing in the Levite camp so as to send him out of it, and [yet] it warns him not to enter, as if he had already gone out. "You have not yet brought him in" — that is to say, it has not yet spoken about his entry, what is to become of it — "you have sent him out," and it spoke of him as if he had [already] gone out. Another version, we read: "You have not yet sent him out, you have brought him in": you have not yet required him to leave the Levite camp, and already you have warned him not to enter, and this is [the meaning of] "you have brought him in" — you are already speaking of his entry.

Rashi on Pesachim 68a:7:2.hebrew: אלא אימא הכי ויצא אל מחוץ למחנה זו מחנה לויה - וכשבא לצאת ממנה, אל יכנס במחנה שכינה. ואי לא הוו כתיבי שתי מחנות, הוה מוקמינא ליה בעומד במחנה שכינה ומצריכו לצאת ממנה, אבל עומד במחנה לויה אין משתלח; והשתא דכתבינן שתי מחנות, על כרחיך הכי תוקמא:
Rashi on Pesachim 68a:7:2.english: Rather, say it thus: “And he shall go outside the camp” — this [is] the Levite camp - And when he comes to leave it, he shall not enter the camp of the Divine Presence. And if two camps had not been written, I would have established it [as referring] to one standing in the camp of the Divine Presence, requiring him to leave it, whereas one standing in the Levite camp would not be sent out; but now that two camps are written, perforce it must be established thus.

Rashi on Pesachim 68a:8:1.english: If so - let [the verse] say, "And they shall send [them] out of the camp, and he shall not come within," and be silent.

Rashi on Pesachim 68a:9:1.hebrew: מנקבן בסכין - שיצא הרעי, שאם יניחנו בתוכן יסריחו קודם שתחשך. ולשון מיחוי, שמוציא פרש רכה דנמחת בתוכה — דשנפי"ר בלע"ז — כמו וממחה ושופך (מעשר שני פ"ה מ"א), וכמו המחהו וגמעו (לעיל פסחים דף לה.). לישנא אחרינא: מיחוי, לשון נקיבה וחיבול, כמו תמחה את זכר עמלק (דברים כ״ה:י״ט):
Rashi on Pesachim 68a:9:1.english: He punctures them with a knife - So that the excrement exits, for if he leaves it inside them, they will become putrid before it gets dark. And the term miḥui [means] that he removes soft excrement that dissolves inside it — desenpir in Old French — like "and he dissolves [it] and pours [it] out" (Maaser Sheni 5:1), and like "he dissolved it and swallowed it" (above, Pesachim 35a). Another explanation: miḥui is an expression of piercing and wounding, like "you shall blot out the remembrance of Amalek" (Deuteronomy 25:19).

Rashi on Pesachim 68a:9:2.hebrew: שירקא דמעיא - ליחה האדוקה במעים שיוצא מהן בדוחק בסכין, ובלע"ז לימו"ן. מיחוי — לשון דבר בזוי, כדמפרש טעמא: "וחרבות מחים":
Rashi on Pesachim 68a:9:2.english: Shirka dime'aya - Moisture that clings to the intestines, which comes out of them through pressure with a knife, and in Old French, limon [slime]. Michui is an expression [denoting] something despised, as [the Gemara] explains the reason: "and the ruins of the fat ones [mechim]."

Tosafot on Pesachim 68a:1:1.hebrew: האי טומאת שבעה כתיב ביה והאי טומאת כו' - הוי מצי לשנויי כדמשני בפ"ק דיומא (דף ו:), דלעולם לטומאת שבעה, וסיפא איצטריכא ליה — "אלא שחמור הימנו בועל נדה, שמטמא משכב ומושב לטמא אוכלין ומשקין":
Tosafot on Pesachim 68a:1:1.english: Seven-day impurity is written about this one, and [seven-day] impurity, etc. - [The Gemara] could have answered as it answers in the first chapter of Yoma (6b): that really [the comparison is] with regard to seven-day impurity, and the latter clause [of the Mishnah] was necessary for it — "except that one who has relations with a menstruating woman is more stringent than him, in that he conveys impurity to a couch or seat to render food and liquids impure."
